operator.payload: Should the table-selection flags be named `--field <name>` and `--field-id <id>` (both repeatable), with requested columns appended after the existing ID column in the order supplied?
operator.answer: OPERATOR_ANSWER: Yes. Use repeatable `--field <name>` and `--field-id <id>` flags; append selected columns after the existing ID column in request order.

operator.payload: If the same field is selected more than once (including once by name and once by ID), should it appear as repeated columns or be shown only once?
operator.answer: OPERATOR_ANSWER: Repeated selections produce repeated columns in the supplied order. Selecting by name and ID in the same invocation is invalid because those flag forms are mutually exclusive.

operator.payload:
Add repeatable `--field <name>` and `--field-id <id>` flags to `gh project item-list`. The flags are mutually exclusive: any invocation containing both forms returns a flag-validation error before listing data. Each repeated occurrence remains a separate requested column, preserving supplied order. Requested columns are appended after the existing `ID` column, and use each field’s canonical project name as the header.

For either form, resolve every requested field against the project fields already returned by the normal `ProjectItems` query, with no separate preflight request. `--field` uses case-insensitive exact name matching; no match returns an actionable error listing available field names, and multiple case-insensitive matches return an ambiguity error directing the user to `--field-id` with matching IDs. `--field-id` uses exact ID matching; no match returns an actionable error listing available `name (id)` candidates. Resolve selections before output, including formatted output, so invalid selections never silently produce an incorrect column.

For each item and selected field, find its returned field value by field ID. Render empty cells for unset values. Render scalar values directly; render iteration and milestone values by title; render labels, users, reviewers, pull requests, and other multi-value field types as readable comma-separated values; render repository values as their URL. Existing default table columns, JSON/export behavior, query support, empty-project errors, and invocations without either new flag remain unchanged.

Add command parsing tests for repeatability and mutual exclusion, table-output tests covering name/ID selection ordering, case-insensitive matching, repeated fields, unset values, every returned field-value type, and error cases. Confirm the selected-field path uses only the existing owner lookup and project-items request. Run focused package tests and the appropriate broader Go test suite before completion.
operator.answer:
DESIGN_CHANGES_REQUIRED

- Explicit formatted/JSON output combined with either field-selection flag must fail clearly; it must not attempt resolution or proceed with formatted output.
- When field definitions have additional pages and fields were requested, retrieve the complete definition list before resolution. Do not paginate when no fields were requested.
- Normalize selected values by removing carriage returns and replacing newlines with spaces.
- Number values must use compact decimal formatting without forced trailing zeros.
- Ambiguous name diagnostics must identify candidate IDs in deterministic order.

When field selection is requested and that definition connection indicates further pages, fetch and append only the remaining pages using its returned cursor, then resolve against the complete definition list. Do not paginate field definitions when no selection flag is present. Thus a project whose definitions fit in the normal response requires no extra field lookup/preflight request, while selections remain correct for projects with more field-definition pages.

For every item and selected field ID, find the corresponding returned field value; absent/unset values render as empty cells. Convert values to human-readable text: dates, text, and select values directly; iterations and milestones by title; numbers with compact decimal formatting and no forced trailing zeroes; labels, users, reviewers, pull requests, and other multi-value types joined with commas; repositories by URL. Before table output, normalize every selected value by stripping carriage returns and replacing newlines with spaces, including values inside multi-value fields. Unknown returned value types render empty rather than misleading data.

Add parsing tests for repeatability, mutual exclusion, and format rejection; output tests for selection order, duplicate selections, case-insensitive names, empty values, newline normalization, compact number formatting, and all returned field-value types; diagnostics tests for missing IDs/names and deterministic ambiguity IDs; and request tests proving no additional field request for a single-page definition list and correct additional-page retrieval only when selection is requested. Run focused and broader Go tests before completion.
